note: Pod inference session 3, RTX 4090. Adds (a) the F1 cross-score putting both selected checkpoints on a common reference, and (b) kid/pr backfill for g_clean at kimg 403-1612 where only fid existed. Diagonal entries are copied from the in-training metric jsonl, not recomputed.

cross_score_f1.reading: The three metrics do not agree on an ordering. fid: each generator is best on its own reference. kid: g_leak lower on BOTH references. precision: g_clean higher on BOTH references. Margins (2e-4 kid, 0.64 fid) are inside what a 111-image reference resolves. Conclusion: contamination produced no detectable difference in distributional sample quality; the generators cannot be ordered.

f3_control.claim: At kimg 806 the contaminated arm collapsed (precision 0.337->0.0003, kid 0.0271->0.0673, fid 61.79->92.77) while the matched clean arm improved on all three (precision 0.428->0.474, kid 0.0282->0.0248, fid 62.06->58.40). The runs differ only in --data. g_leak recovered by kimg 1209: an instability episode, not a failed run.
f3_control.caveat: GAN_SEEDS=[0]. One seed per arm, so this is co-occurrence, not established causation.
